text: It was not worth the while of a man who esteemed turnips a most delicate food, and who boiled them himself, whilst his wife made bread, to brag so often of a halfpenny, and write a book to show how a man may soonest grow rich; the very good of being contented with little is because it cuts off at once the desire and the anxiety for superfluities.
author: Plutarch
locator: Comparison of Aristides with Marcus Cato
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
